what_it_is.prose: Airbus Defence and Space is the defence and space division of European aerospace group Airbus SE. Its principal Indian military-aerospace footprint is the C-295 (C-295 MW) medium tactical transport programme for the Indian Air Force. Signed on 24 September 2021 for ₹21,935 crore (~US$2.5 billion), the programme covers 56 aircraft to replace the IAF's legacy Avro HS-748 fleet: 16 delivered fly-away from Airbus's Seville facility in Spain (deliveries began September 2023) and 40 assembled in India by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) at a dedicated Final Assembly Line (FAL) in Vadodara, Gujarat. The Vadodara FAL — inaugurated on 28 October 2024 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez — is the first private-sector military aircraft final assembly line in India, and the first India-built C-295 was rolled out in a milestone announced in October 2025. Airbus states the programme will deliver more than 85% of the structural and final-assembly work of the 40 India-build aircraft locally, with roughly 13,000 detail parts manufactured in India and 37 Indian suppliers onboarded across the public and private sectors; all 40 India-assembled aircraft are targeted for completion by August 2031. The C-295 carries up to 9 tonnes / 71 troops, ranges to ~5,000 km, and is powered by two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127 engines. Beyond the C-295, Airbus maintains engineering centres in Bengaluru and a large commercial-aviation and helicopter business in India; this dossier focuses on the military-aerospace (C-295) footprint and does not infer an indigenous-content percentage for the imported engines and avionics.

deployments_procurement.summary: Airbus's India military-aerospace activity is anchored by the 56-aircraft C-295 programme (₹21,935 crore, 2021). The first 16 aircraft are imported fly-away from Seville (deliveries from September 2023); the remaining 40 are assembled by TASL at the Vadodara FAL, inaugurated October 2024, with the first India-built aircraft rolled out per an October 2025 milestone and completion targeted by August 2031.

faq.question: What is Airbus Defence and Space's main military-aerospace footprint in India?
faq.answer: The Indian Air Force's 56-aircraft C-295 transport programme, signed on 24 September 2021 for ₹21,935 crore (~US$2.5 billion). Sixteen aircraft are imported fly-away from Airbus's Seville facility in Spain and 40 are assembled in India by Tata Advanced Systems Limited (TASL) at a Final Assembly Line in Vadodara, Gujarat — the first private-sector military aircraft FAL in India, inaugurated on 28 October 2024.

faq.question: How much of the C-295 is being built in India?
faq.answer: Airbus states that more than 85% of the structural and final-assembly work on the 40 India-build C-295s is done locally, with roughly 13,000 detail parts manufactured in India and 37 Indian suppliers onboarded across the public and private sectors. The first Make-in-India C-295 was rolled out per an October 2025 milestone, and all 40 India-assembled aircraft are targeted for completion by August 2031. The two Pratt & Whitney Canada PW127 engines and much of the avionics remain imported.

faq.question: What is the C-295 replacing in IAF service?
faq.answer: The C-295 replaces the Indian Air Force's legacy Avro HS-748 transport fleet. It provides tactical airlift for troop and paratroop transport, logistics, and casualty evacuation, carrying up to 9 tonnes or 71 troops with a range of about 5,000 km.
